newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares go into reverse, shed 1.94 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares go into reverse, shed 1.94 pct.

text.p: Greek shares pulled back 1.94 percent on Tuesday, ending a four-day winning streak which added nearly 100 points to the general share index.
Brokers said investors lost their earlier enthusiasm on news sparked by strong profitability in the banking sector, but noted that price corrections were part of the game.
"Investors probably over-reacted to a feel-good factor provided by announcements of upbeat interim results of banks," said Harry Mathiopoulos, a broker at Intersec.
Since last Thursday, a number of banks including market leaders National Bank and Alpha Credit, along with ErgoBank, NIBID and Xiosbank have posted strong half-year profit growth.
"With the market having soared during 1997 and considerable gains recorded in the past few days, a price correction should not come as a surprise to anyone," Mathiopoulos said.
Investors were advised by Intersec's Mathiopoulos to look for long-term prospects in view of increased market volatility.
"There is low trading volume which coupled with the market's increased volatility within the 1,450-1,620 trading range renders these trading patterns fairly usual," said Mathiopoulos.
Market-participants should place more emphasis when picking stocks on long-term prospects, which remain good, and refrain from impulse-buying and short-term plays, he added.
The Athens general index settled 1.94 percent or 31.43 points lower at 1,592.01 from Monday's 1,623.44 close, recovering just before the close from the day's low of 1,588.33 recorded in late trade.
All sector sub-indices settled lower, with banks and industrials leading with losses of 1.94 and 2.38 percent respectively.
Turnover was depressed, reaching 11.8 billion drachmas on volume of 3.3 million shares.
Block trading included 50,000 shares of OTE telecom which changed hands at 6,400 drachmas.
Decliners beat advancers 163 to 45 with 15 shares unchanged on 223 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.5-$10.9. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,123-1,153 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,049-1,109 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock lost 115 drachmas to 6,265.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 639.42-680.23 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $74.96-$77.78. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,643-3,684 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.61 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 235-266 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
